title: Under the Seal: Confirming Magna Carta, 1297
description: A source-grounded historical adventure in which a chancery clerk hears rival claims as Edward I confirms Magna Carta.
learningObjectives: Explain what Magna Carta promised about justice, taxation, and the rights of free men.
Describe why barons, church, and king each wanted the charter confirmed or resisted.
Evaluate whose interests the charter protected most strongly.

player.name: Unnamed Clerk
player.brief: You record arguments, inspect draft copies, and prepare minutes before the king's confirmation is entered.

sharedContext.text: Edward I has renewed the Great Charter at Westminster, and the bargain joins liberties to a grant of taxation. As a chancery clerk, you must hear the claims of king, clergy, barons, and other free subjects before the final wording is entered.

spans.quote: For this gift and grant of these liberties and of others contained in our charter over the liberties of the forest, the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, earls, barons, knights, fee holders and all of our realm have given us a fifteenth part of all their movable goods.
We, holding these aforesaid gifts and grants to be right and welcome, conceed and confirm them for ourselves and our heirs and by the terms of the present (letters) renew them

assumptions.text: The player is an unnamed clerk in the royal chancery who can hear petitions and prepare draft minutes.
assumptions.rationale: The teacher brief specifies the student role, but the source text does not mention such a clerk.

assumptions.text: The adventure compresses the process of consultation, drafting, and sealing into three linked encounters on the way to confirmation.
assumptions.rationale: The source gives the confirmed text, not the step-by-step process that produced it.

assumptions.text: Stage 0 uses an imagined chancery hall, archive, and office inside Westminster.
assumptions.rationale: The source names Westminster but does not describe interior rooms.

assumptions.text: Stage 1 uses an imagined consultation route through a courtyard, chapel, office, and hall within Westminster.
assumptions.rationale: The source does not describe where different groups waited or argued.

assumptions.text: Stage 2 uses imagined final drafting rooms near the place where the royal seal is prepared.
assumptions.rationale: The source records confirmation, not the exact physical setting of final drafting.

assumptions.text: Large groups named in the charter are represented by single speaking envoys for gameplay clarity.
assumptions.rationale: The source names estates and corporate bodies, not the individual spokesmen in this scenario.

assumptions.text: Private motives, hidden interests, and limits of knowledge are inferred from the liberties each group defends.
assumptions.rationale: The charter states public grants and protections, but not inner thoughts.

assumptions.text: Evidence items are playable working copies and excerpts lifted from the charter text for inspection.
assumptions.rationale: The game needs inspectable objects, while the source provides only the full document.

summary.text: The crown issues the letters, confirms the charter, and receives a fifteenth in return. Royal authority is not absent from the text; it frames the whole act of confirmation.

spans.quote: Edward by the grace of God King of England, lord of Ireland and duke of Aquitaine sends greetings to all to whom the present letters come.

summary.text: The charter places church liberty first and later preserves liberties and customs to ecclesiastical as well as secular holders.

endings.title: The Charter Confirmed
endings.summary: Your draft becomes a full confirmation. The language of renewal and durable observance stands, and the bargain looks solemn as well as political.

historicalOutcome.text: This matches the record closely. The charter says the realm gave the king a fifteenth, and Edward then confirmed and renewed the grants, wishing the charter to be firmly observed in perpetuity.

spans.quote: For this gift and grant of these liberties and of others contained in our charter over the liberties of the forest, the archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, earls, barons, knights, fee holders and all of our realm have given us a fifteenth part of all their movable goods.

endings.divergence: This ending is the closest match to the source record.

endings.title: A Narrow Settlement
endings.summary: Your record reduces the moment to custom and payment. The charter survives, but it sounds less like a broad standard of justice and more like a negotiated exchange.

historicalOutcome.text: The source record is broader than this. It links the fifteenth to the grant, but it also states that Edward confirmed and renewed the charter and wished it to be firmly observed.

endings.divergence: This differs from the record because the surviving text confirms all the charter's articles, not merely a thin bargain over revenue and custom.

endings.title: The Entry Delayed
endings.summary: You hold the draft back. Arguments continue, but delay weakens trust, and every side fears that time will favor someone else.

historicalOutcome.text: The source suggests no such pause. It presents completed letters patent, witnessed at Westminster, and states that Edward confirmed and renewed the charter.

endings.title: Royal Resistance Prevails
endings.summary: You advise against binding language. The crown keeps room to manoeuvre, but the political cost is sharp, because every estate can see what was almost promised and withheld.

historicalOutcome.text: This is opposite to the source. The surviving text shows Edward confirming and renewing the charter rather than refusing it.
